glosses: One from whom a person is descended, whether on the father's or mother's side, at any distance of time; a progenitor; a forefather; a forebear.

examples.text: Whether modern, industrial man is less or more warlike than his hunter-gatherer ancestors is impossible to determine. The machine gun is so much more lethal than the bow and arrow that comparisons are meaningless.

glosses: An earlier type; a progenitor

examples.text: This fossil animal is regarded as the ancestor of the horse.

glosses: One from whom an estate has descended;—the correlative of heir.
One who had the same role or function in former times.

examples.text: The Magpies are unbeaten and enjoying their best run since 1994, although few would have thought the class of 2011 would come close to emulating their ancestors.

glosses: A word or phrase which serves as the origin of a term in another language.

examples.text: Le culte de l’ancêtre doit beaucoup à l’intérêt commercial. En se proclamant descendants de l’inventrice du camembert, les petits-enfants de Marie Harel s’attribuaient un label d’authenticité et de tradition.
